output.brief: Don't roll back gateway 5.8. The evidence points to the 2 Nov storage compaction tuning change, not the gateway. In 11 cells the push raised compaction threads from 2 to 6, and disk use jumped from 41% to 97% within 5 minutes. Disk read wait rose from 9 to 205 ms. Latency crossed 150 ms within minutes of the push in each cell, whatever gateway version the cell was running. The eu-w cells were still on 5.7 when they degraded. Cell aps-3 skipped the push during a change freeze but did get 5.8, and it stayed at about 94 ms. Rolling euw-1 back to 5.7 changed nothing (291 → 297 → 293 ms). The network looks clean, and traffic growth is small. A rollback would also reopen the signature vulnerability and add about 4 hours of churn without fixing latency. I'm fairly confident, about 90%. Next steps: revert the tuning in one cell and watch p99 and backlog, then extend to the other cells. Don't pause compaction. The backlog got high (11.2% on 2 Nov) from sources not yet attributed (Orrin migration, expiry sweep), so wait for the 10 Nov attribution before limiting Orrin's ingest. Gateway CPU profiling is a reasonable low-priority task.
